messages:
maya: quick heads up — after yesterday's kernel-routing tweak i'm seeing p99 tail spikes on small-encoder runs. p50 unchanged. noticed ~+150-200ms on 2xA10 nodes during microbursts. can we triage?

chen: saw this too. quick numbers from a perf trace: p50 42ms -> 44ms, p95 88ms -> 112ms, p99 120ms -> 304ms. profile highlights: kernel_switches +37%, avg_queue_delay 7.9ms -> 15.3ms, kv_hit_rate 91% -> 79%. attaching inline snippet.

sam: initial hunch: batching heuristics + new kernel fallback are interacting. when max_batch_tokens high we form large microbatches that shift sequence-length distribution and trigger cold kernels more often. also saw more KV cold-starts during tail events.

gabi: confirmed kv miss spike correlates: eviction_policy changed to lru-clock last week — likely increased churn for short prefixes. log snippet: `KV_CACHE.EVICT items=842 delta_evicted=73 window_ms=6000` then several requests fell back to full KV load.

perf-bot: ci/perf small-encoder baseline: p99=118ms (ref build 2026-02-11). current branch: p99=302ms (+184ms). running short sweep with three configs now. results queued.

chen: propose controlled sweep matrix rather than ad-hoc: vary `max_batch_tokens` [1024, 2048, 4096], `max_wait_ms` [4, 8, 16], and `kv_cache_capacity` [128MB, 256MB]. also compare `kernel_routing` modes: `heuristic-v2` vs `seq-pref`. aim to capture p50/p95/p99, kernel_switch_count, avg_queue_delay, kv_hit_rate, and token throughput.

maya: +1. prioritize combos that reduce p99 under 250ms while keeping throughput drop <10%. can we run a first canary on 2048/8/256?

sam: i'll run the canary with target qps=200 and populate per-route histograms. running command:

```
# run canary on canary-3
./perf_run --model small-encoder --qps 200 \
  --max_batch_tokens 2048 --max_wait_ms 8 \
  --kv_cache_capacity 256MB --kernel_routing heuristic-v2 \
  --collect metrics:histograms,kv,hits,queue_delay
```

sam: ETA ~20m. i'll capture kernel traces (`KERNEL_SWITCH_TRACE`) and attach after.

gabi: add alerts on console: p99 > 250ms and kv_hit_rate < 80% for the canary ID, otherwise auto-fail. dashboard to watch: rrt/perf/small-encoder (link: https://console/redwood/dashboards/rrt/perf/small-encoder).

chen: small note: when comparing kernel variants, check for cold-kernel init cost — some fallbacks add ~30-60ms on first use. include a warmup step in the sweep: `--warmup-seconds 60`.

maya: good catch. include warmup. sam, add warmup and then run each combo for 3 minutes steady-state after warmup. record both warmup and steady windows.

perf-bot: sweep update: first canary (2048/8/256) steady-state p99=238ms, p95=118ms, avg_queue_delay=9.7ms, kv_hit_rate=83%. kernel_switch_count reduced vs baseline but still higher than golden.

chen: promising — p99 under 250ms. compare to 1024/4: that one looked like p99=210ms but throughput dropped ~12% (batching inefficiency). 4096/16 gives best throughput but p99 back up >320ms due to longer queue delays.

sam: summary so far: tradeoff surface is clear: smaller max_batch_tokens reduces tail but hurts throughput; slightly higher max_wait_ms can amortize kernel overhead without increasing tail too much if kv_hit stays healthy. also kv capacity bump to 256MB helped hit-rate and smoothed tails.

gabi: follow-up action: roll back the eviction tweak to previous policy in a canary so we can isolate kernel-routing vs kv churn. i've drafted a rollout plan.

maya: action items: sam runs a full sweep on the matrix with warmup and steady windows, chen will analyze kernel traces and produce tail heatmap, gabi will revert eviction policy in canary and compare kv metrics. i'll watch console and hold the production rollout until we have a config that meets p99 < 250ms and throughput loss < 10%. assign owners accordingly. :thumbsup:

sam: on it — kicking off full sweep now. will post results thread when done.

chen: i'll start an analysis doc after sam's run. trying a new flamegraph for kernel switch hot paths.

gabi: i'll also add a temporary alert to mute noisy infra alarms during the sweep.

maya: thanks team — nice quick triage.
